title: Cancer-Associated Stroke: Combinatorial Approach to Dysfunctional multi-target signalling modulEs
summary: It is well known, that cancer patients have an elevated risk to develop stroke. In this study, peripheral immune cells from patients with stroke, lung cancer, and lung cancer-associated stroke will be analysed at the gene level to identify alterations that could lead to stroke in lung cancer patients. Furthermore, blood markers for predicting stroke events  in lung cancer patients should be identified. Finally, new therapeutic options will be developed based on the analysis.
conditions: Stroke, not specified as haemorrhage or infarction
Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung

interventions.name:
Group1
Transcriptome analysis of PBMCs isolated from blood of lung cancer patients. Analysis of blood plasma. No interventional analysis.

Group2
Transcriptome analysis of PBMCs isolated from blood of stroke patients. Analysis of blood plasma. No interventional analysis.

Group3
Transcriptome analysis of PBMCs isolated from blood of lung cancer-associated stroke patients. Identification of driver genes leading to stroke events in lung cancer patients. Identification of differences in the transcriptome profil compared to lung cancer only and stroke only patients. Ide

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Stroke event must occur within first year after tumor diagnosis
Exclusion criteria:
autoimmune disorders, immunosuppressant intake
